name: effectiveSize
title: Effective sample size for estimating the mean

origin.details: For a time series x of length N, the standard error of the mean is the square root of var(x)/n where n is the effective sample size. n = N only when there is no autocorrelation. Estimation of the effective sample size requires estimating the spectral density at frequency zero. This is done by the function spectrum0.ar. For an mcmc.list object, the effective sizes are summed across chains.
origin.value: A vector giving the effective sample size for each column of x.
origin.example: n <- 2000; i <- seq_len(n); x <- cbind(sin(i/3)+0.2*cos(i), cos(i/5)+0.01*i, rep(2, n)); y <- cbind(sin(i/4)+0.15*cos(i/2), cos(i/6)+0.005*i, rep(1, n)); cat(paste(sprintf("%.17g", effectiveSize(mcmc.list(mcmc(x), mcmc(y)))), collapse=" "), "\n")

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: One chain, as a vector or a matrix with iterations in rows, or a list of chains. A list of chains is summed.

translation.details: For a time series x of length N, the standard error of the mean is the square root of var(x)/n where n is the effective sample size. n = N only when there is no autocorrelation. Estimation of the effective sample size requires estimating the spectral density at frequency zero. This is done by the function spectrum0.ar. For an mcmc.list object, the effective sizes are summed across chains.
translation.value: A vector giving the effective sample size for each column of x.
translation.example: n = 2000; i = np.arange(1, n + 1, dtype=float); x = np.column_stack((np.sin(i / 3) + 0.2 * np.cos(i), np.cos(i / 5) + 0.01 * i, np.full(n, 2.0))); y = np.column_stack((np.sin(i / 4) + 0.15 * np.cos(i / 2), np.cos(i / 6) + 0.005 * i, np.full(n, 1.0))); print(" ".join(format(float(v), ".17g") for v in effectiveSize([x, y])))
